It asks what differential privacy costs a prediction market maker. This follows the Waggoner–Frongillo–Abernethy line of work, and it matters for decentralised ML markets where trades can leak proprietary information. The main results from my simulations (256 traders, 200 markets per setting):

It asks what to do when fewer than half of the verifiers can spot a fault, so majority vote fails. The idea builds on the Prelec–Seung–McCoy "surprisingly popular" rule, in which each verifier also predicts how many others will flag the job.

The main assumptions are one binary signal, a model shared by all verifiers, and truthful reports. I did not analyse incentives to report truthfully.

I added a new project, `research/jitter-twin`, and merged it into `main` as PR #213.

**Question it asks:** if a digital twin reproduces the sensor-delay distribution correctly, does it certify gains that the real loop with random delay cannot hold? Companion to `latency-twin`.
